areas.n: The Loop & Downtown (River North, Streeterville, Gold Coast, South Loop, Museum Campus, West Loop)
North Side (Lincoln Park, Lakeview, Lincoln Square, Uptown & Argyle, Andersonville, Rogers Park & Devon)
Northwest Side (Wicker Park, Bucktown, Ukrainian Village, Logan Square, Humboldt Park, Avondale, Albany Park)
West Side (Pilsen, Little Village, Little Italy & Taylor St, Garfield Park, Austin)
South Side (Chinatown, Bridgeport, Bronzeville, Hyde Park, Woodlawn, South Shore)

Far South (Pullman, Beverly & Morgan Park, Chatham, Roseland, the Calumet)
Suburbs & North Shore (Evanston, Oak Park, Skokie, Wilmette, Glencoe, Berwyn, the western suburbs)
Day Trips (Indiana Dunes, Starved Rock, Milwaukee, the Lake Michigan shore)

cuisines.n: Hot Dogs, Maxwell Street Polish & Burgers
Fried Chicken, Mild Sauce, BBQ & Soul Food

P.w: One of the world's great art museums — 300,000 works including Seurat's La Grande Jatte, Hopper's Nighthawks and Wood's American Gothic.

P.ad: 1400 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
P.w: The 1893-born natural history museum on the Museum Campus — home of SUE the T. rex and Máximo the titanosaur.
The 103rd-floor observation deck of the former Sears Tower, with The Ledge glass boxes 1,353 ft over Wacker Drive.

P.ad: Millennium Park, 201 E Randolph St, Chicago, IL 60602
P.w: Anish Kapoor's mirror-polished 'Bean' in Millennium Park — the requisite Chicago selfie, beside Gehry's Pritzker Pavilion and the Lurie Garden. Free.
P.k: public art sculpture icon park free

P.w: The 1916 pier stretching into Lake Michigan, with the 200-ft Centennial Wheel, the Chicago Children's Museum and boat departures.
Grant Park's 1927 Versailles-inspired fountain, one of the largest in the world, with summer light-and-water shows. Free.

P.ad: 1300 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
P.w: The first planetarium in the Western Hemisphere (1930), at the tip of Northerly Island's peninsula with a classic skyline view.
The 1869 limestone water tower that survived the Great Chicago Fire, now a free city art gallery on the Mag Mile.

P.ad: 5700 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60637
P.w: The largest science centre in the Western Hemisphere, in the 1893 World's Fair Palace of Fine Arts — U-505 submarine, coal mine, Pioneer Zephyr.
The Cubs' ivy-walled ballpark (1914), the second-oldest in the majors, with its hand-turned scoreboard and Wrigleyville rooftops.

P.ad: 300 N Central Park Ave, Chicago, IL 60624
P.w: Jens Jensen's 1908 'landscape art under glass' — one of the largest conservatories in the US, with free admission.
One of the country's oldest zoos (1868) and still free, with the Farm-in-the-Zoo and Nature Boardwalk.
Frank Lloyd Wright's 1910 Prairie School masterpiece in Hyde Park, inscribed by UNESCO in The 20th-Century Architecture of Frank Lloyd Wright. Tours by the FLW Trust.
P.k: frank lloyd wright prairie school house

P.w: The 1897 former public library, now the nation's first free municipal cultural center — under the world's largest Tiffany glass dome (38 ft, ~30,000 pieces).
Burnham & Root's 1888 LaSalle Street landmark, whose skylit light court was remodelled by Frank Lloyd Wright in 1905 — the spiral oriel staircase is the money shot.
P.k: architecture building frank lloyd wright landmark

P.w: The 1921 French Baroque movie palace under the six-storey C-H-I-C-A-G-O marquee on State Street.

Hood & Howells' 1925 Gothic tower from the 'most beautiful building in the world' competition, its base studded with ~150 fragments of famous buildings (Westminster Abbey, the Great Wall, the Parthenon).
The tapering, X-braced former John Hancock Center (1969), with the 94th-floor 360 Chicago observation deck and TILT.
Bertrand Goldberg's 1963 'corncob' towers on the river — at opening the tallest residential and tallest concrete buildings in the world.
Frank Gehry's ribbon-steel bandshell in Millennium Park — free summer concerts (Grant Park Music Festival) and movies on the lawn.
Frank Lloyd Wright's 1908 poured-concrete temple in Oak Park — part of UNESCO's 20th-Century Architecture of Frank Lloyd Wright inscription.

P.n: Frank Lloyd Wright Home and Studio
P.w: Where Wright lived and worked 1889–1909 and developed the Prairie style; a National Historic Landmark, toured by the Frank Lloyd Wright Trust.
P.k: frank lloyd wright prairie school house

P.ad: 11141 S Cottage Grove Ave, Chicago, IL 60628
P.w: George Pullman's 1880s company town — the clock-tower factory, Hotel Florence and rowhouses; site of the 1894 strike and the Pullman porters' story. NPS unit since 2015.
The lace-domed 1953 Baháʼí temple on the Wilmette lakefront — the oldest surviving Baháʼí House of Worship in the world, with formal gardens.
Pilsen's free museum of Mexican art — one of the largest Latinx cultural institutions in the US (10,000+ works); its Día de Muertos show is a city ritual.
Founded 1961 in Washington Park — the oldest independent African American museum in the country.
One of the largest contemporary art museums in the world, in Streeterville off the Mag Mile; Tuesday summer jazz on the terrace.
The city's history museum at the south end of Lincoln Park — Lincoln's deathbed, the Great Fire, and an exhibit on the Chicago hot dog.
Chicago's oldest and largest continuously running blues club (1968) — two stages, alternating sets until 4 a.m.
The South Loop blues club owned by Buddy Guy himself — live blues every night and his own January residency.
One of the city's best-known jazz rooms, two blocks off the Mag Mile, with nightly sets and jam sessions.
Uptown's 1907 former Capone-era speakeasy, one of the oldest continuously operating jazz clubs in the country; home of the Uptown Poetry Slam.
P.k: jazz club speakeasy cocktail bar music

P.w: Old Town's improv theatre (1959) that launched Belushi, Murray, Fey, Colbert and Carell.

P.n: ISAC Museum (Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures)
P.ad: University of Chicago campus, Hyde Park (per Wikipedia)
P.w: The University of Chicago's free museum of the ancient Near East (ex-Oriental Institute) — a 40-ton Assyrian lamassu, Egyptian mummies, Persepolis reliefs.

P.ad: Washington Park community area, Chicago (per Wikipedia)
P.w: Olmsted & Vaux's 372-acre South Side park, home of Lorado Taft's 'Fountain of Time' and the DuSable museum.

P.ad: Evanston lakefront, IL (per NPS NHL record)
P.w: Château-style 1894 lakefront mansion of Nobel laureate and US Vice President Charles G. Dawes — a National Historic Landmark run by the Evanston History Center.
385 acres on nine islands in the Cook County Forest Preserves at Glencoe — 24 gardens, prairies and greenhouses; the winter Orchid Show.
The 216-acre Chicago Zoological Park in Brookfield — polar bears, the Seven Seas dolphins, Tropic World.
The 2.7-mile elevated rail-trail through Logan Square, Humboldt Park, Wicker Park and Bucktown. Free.

P.ad: 6401 S Stony Island Ave (Wooded Island, Jackson Park), Chicago, IL 60637
P.w: The Japanese garden on Jackson Park's Wooded Island, rooted in Japan's 1893 World's Fair pavilion; 160 cherry trees in spring. Free.
Victorian garden cemetery (1860) of Chicago's builders — Burnham, Sullivan, Mies, Marshall Field, Roger Ebert — with Lorado Taft's 'Eternal Silence'.
The Bears' colonnaded 1924 lakefront stadium (with its 2003 'spaceship' bowl), also home of the Chicago Fire.

P.n: Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures Museum
P.w: The University of Chicago's free museum of the ancient Near East (ex-Oriental Institute) — the 40-ton Khorsabad lamassu, Egypt, Persia, Mesopotamia.
The University of Chicago's soaring Gothic chapel, with a 72-bell carillon among the largest instruments ever built.

P.ad: 5491 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60615
P.w: Alfred Caldwell's limestone-stepped peninsula with a castle-like field house — a downtown-skyline view, swimming off the rocks and fire pits. Free.

P.ad: 7059 S South Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60649
P.w: The 1906 South Shore Country Club, now a Park District cultural center with a beach, nature sanctuary and golf — the Obamas held their wedding reception here.
H. H. Richardson's 1887 Romanesque fortress-house on Prairie Avenue, a museum of the Gilded Age.

P.ad: 50 E Ida B. Wells Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
P.w: Adler & Sullivan's 1889 Auditorium Building — a National Historic Landmark with a gold-leafed arched hall and famous acoustics.
Burnham & Root's 1891 load-bearing brick skyscraper — 'the first modern building' — with Holabird & Roche's steel-frame 1893 addition.
The 1925 Beaux-Arts station whose Great Hall rises under a 219-ft barrel-vaulted skylight — the Untouchables staircase.
The 1890s Victorian glasshouse in Lincoln Park — palms, ferns and orchids, free and open year-round.
15 miles of Lake Michigan beaches and towering dunes an hour from the Loop by the South Shore Line — Mount Baldy, the West Beach dune trails.
Sandstone canyons and seasonal waterfalls on the Illinois River, 90 minutes south-west of Chicago — Illinois's most-visited state park.
The two surviving buildings of Jane Addams's 1889 settlement house on the UIC campus — the birthplace of American social work. Free (suggested donation).
North America's oldest outdoor music festival — the Chicago Symphony's summer home; picnic on the lawn.
1,700 acres of trees in Lisle with 16 miles of trails and a children's garden; Illumination in winter.

P.ad: 700 N Art Museum Dr, Milwaukee, WI 53202
P.w: Calatrava's lakefront Quadracci Pavilion whose Burke Brise Soleil 'wings' open and close daily — 90 minutes north of Chicago.
The only Harley-Davidson Museum in the world — 450+ motorcycles on a 20-acre Menomonee Valley campus.
Louis Sullivan's only intact house of worship (1903), a Russian-village church in Ukrainian Village, part-funded by Tsar Nicholas II.

P.ad: 3100 W Logan Blvd (Logan Square), Chicago, IL 60647
P.w: The eagle-topped column at the heart of Logan Square (1918), by Henry Bacon of the Lincoln Memorial — the hub of the boulevard system.
One of the oldest and largest ethnic museums in the US (1935), in the old Polish Downtown.
Rapp & Rapp's 1925 'acre of seats in a magic city' — the largest movie palace ever built in Chicago, shuttered since 1981 and awaiting restoration (exterior only).
The 1926 Spanish-palace dance hall with a twinkling-star ceiling, now a rock venue.
The 1929 Southport movie palace with a starry-sky ceiling and a live organist between shows — Chicago's leading independent cinema.
The 1914 Lincoln Avenue movie house outside which John Dillinger was shot by the FBI in 1934; now Victory Gardens' stage.

P.ad: Washington Park, 5900 S Cottage Grove Ave, Chicago, IL 60637
P.w: Lorado Taft's 1922 concrete procession of 100 figures passing before Father Time, at the west end of the Midway. Free.

P.ad: 6760 S Stony Island Ave, Chicago, IL 60649
P.w: Theaster Gates's restored 1923 bank — the Johnson Publishing library, Frankie Knuckles' records, galleries and free events.
P.k: gallery arts library house music free

P.w: Mies van der Rohe's 1956 glass-and-steel architecture school at IIT — widely held to be his finest work; a National Historic Landmark.

P.ad: 3500 S Dr Martin Luther King Jr Dr, Chicago, IL 60653
P.w: Bronzeville's 1928 memorial to the Black 8th Illinois regiment (370th Infantry) of WWI, won by a Chicago Defender campaign.
The 1879 Burnham & Root limestone gate — all that remains of the 475-acre Union Stock Yards that made Chicago 'hog butcher for the world'. A National Historic Landmark; free.
Where Martin Luther King Jr. marched for open housing in 1966 (and was struck by a rock); the Living Memorial's three pillars at Marquette Rd & Kedzie tell the Fair Housing story. Free.
The only museum in North America devoted to Lithuanian history and culture — in the city with the most Lithuanians outside Lithuania.

P.ad: Millennium Park, 201 E Randolph St, Chicago, IL 60602
P.w: Jaume Plensa's twin 50-ft glass-block towers in Millennium Park, projecting faces of Chicagoans who spout water into the splash pool. Free.
P.k: fountain public art park free family

P.ad: Daley Plaza, 50 W Washington St, Chicago, IL 60602
P.w: Picasso's untitled 50-ft Cor-ten steel sculpture (1967) in Daley Plaza — baboon, woman or dog, he never said. Free.

P.ad: Federal Plaza, 50 W Adams St, Chicago, IL 60603
P.w: Alexander Calder's 53-ft red stabile (1974) set against Mies van der Rohe's black Federal Center. Free.

P.ad: Chase Tower Plaza, 10 S Dearborn St, Chicago, IL 60603
P.w: Marc Chagall's 70-ft mosaic box (1974) of six Chicago scenes in 250 colours. Free.
20 acres east of Millennium Park — the climbing walls, the winter skating ribbon, mini golf and a giant playground. Free.

P.ad: Chicago River (main branch), Lake St to Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60601
P.w: The 1.25-mile path along the river's main branch — wine bars, kayak rentals and the city's best architecture at water level. Free.
Independent research library (1887) facing Washington Square — free exhibitions from 1.6 million books and 600,000 maps.
The world's largest public library building at opening (1991), with owl-topped acroterions and a 9th-floor winter garden. Free.
Chinatown's riverside park on an old rail yard — pagoda pavilion, kayak launch and the water-taxi stop. Free.
Small Chinatown museum on the Chinese journey to the Midwest, in the old Quong Yick warehouse.
Pilsen's 1892 hall modelled on the Prague opera house, now one of the city's favourite music venues (with Dusek's downstairs).
The Sunday open-air flea market descended from the 1880s Maxwell Street bazaar — tools, tires, produce and some of the city's best street tacos.
The Chicago Academy of Sciences' museum in Lincoln Park, built around the 2,700-sq-ft Judy Istock Butterfly Haven.

P.ad: Montrose Harbor (W Montrose Ave & Lake Shore Dr), Chicago, IL 60640
P.w: 15 lakefront acres where 300+ migratory species stop at 'the Magic Hedge'. Free.
Col. Robert McCormick's 500-acre Wheaton estate — gardens, his mansion, and the First Division tank museum.

P.n: Illinois Holocaust Museum and Education Center
P.w: Stanley Tigerman's Skokie museum founded by survivors, with its pioneering interactive survivor-hologram theatre.

P.ad: 339 N Oak Park Ave, Oak Park, IL 60302
P.w: The Queen Anne house where Hemingway was born in 1899, restored as a museum.
Evanston's 1873 lighthouse on the lake bluff, a National Historic Landmark; summer weekend tours.

P.ad: Forest Home Cemetery, 863 S Des Plaines Ave, Forest Park, IL 60130
P.w: The 1893 monument over the graves of the executed Haymarket anarchists — a pilgrimage site for May Day; surrounded by 'Radical Row'. National Historic Landmark.

P.ad: 373 W Geneva St, Williams Bay, WI 53191
P.w: The 1897 'birthplace of modern astrophysics' on Geneva Lake — home of the world's largest refracting telescope; tours.
Frank Lloyd Wright's 1939 'dendriform'-columned Great Workroom and Research Tower in Racine — free tours by reservation.

P.ad: 1600 N Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60614
P.w: Chicago's busiest beach, by Lincoln Park — the ocean-liner beach house, volleyball, paddleboards and the classic skyline-across-the-sand view. Free.

P.ad: 1000 N Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60611
P.w: The Gold Coast beach at the top of the Mag Mile, tucked under the skyline. Free.

P.ad: 1200 S Linn White Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
P.w: Small crescent beach on Northerly Island behind the Adler, with panoramic lake views. Free.

P.ad: 1521 S Linn White Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
P.w: The man-made peninsula (the old Meigs Field) re-wilded with prairie paths, fishing spots and skyline views. Free.
Jens Jensen's 207-acre park — the Prairie School boathouse and swan boats on the lagoon, and the 1895 stables now housing the National Museum of Puerto Rican Arts & Culture. Free.
Ukrainian Village museum of folk art, pysanky (Easter eggs) and immigrant history.
The domed 1892 French-Romanesque church of the city's old French parish, in Little Italy/University Village.
The presidential museum, library branch and tower in Jackson Park, opened Juneteenth (June 19) 2026 — timed tickets sold out months ahead.
The 1924 white-terracotta twin towers with a Giralda-style clock tower — the first skyscraper on the new Michigan Avenue, floodlit at night.
Holabird & Root's 1930 Art Deco tower closing the LaSalle Street canyon, crowned by John Storrs's faceless aluminium Ceres.
The Archdiocese's 1875 Gothic Revival cathedral by Patrick Keely, with the cardinals' galeros hanging from the ceiling.
Frank Lloyd Wright's 1915 cubic Prairie house in Rogers Park — tours via the FLW Trust, and you can even stay overnight.
P.k: frank lloyd wright prairie school house

P.w: Andersonville's 1976 museum of Swedish immigrant history and art, with a children's immigration museum upstairs.
Rapp & Rapp's 1917 Balaban & Katz movie palace in the Uptown theatre district, now a rock venue.
The 1912 Victoria vaudeville house in Lakeview, now a concert hall that has hosted Bowie, Pearl Jam and Coldplay.

P.ad: Longwood Dr & W 103rd St (Beverly), Chicago, IL 60643
P.w: One of the largest urban districts on the National Register — 3,000+ homes on the glacial ridge of Beverly and Morgan Park by Wright, Maher, Griffin, Burnham and Shaw; walk Longwood Drive past the Givins 'Irish castle'. Free.
P.k: historic district architecture house frank lloyd wright prairie school free

P.w: Third Ward food hall of ~20 vendors — brats, squeaky cheese curds, seafood, Thai — named one of America's best public markets by Frommer's.
Riverside craft brewery (1987) that helped revive Milwaukee brewing — its comic tour and Friday fish fry are city rituals.
Captain Frederick Pabst's 1892 Flemish Renaissance Revival mansion, restored and open for tours.
Lakeshore science-and-technology museum with the Reiman Aquarium and a tall ship.
The 1860 Gothic Revival church that survived the Great Fire (the O'Learys were parishioners) — the second-oldest Catholic church in Chicago.
Garfield Park's 1902 Renaissance Revival basilica with a gold-leafed barrel vault — one of three papal basilicas in Chicago (WTTW's 'Most Beautiful Places').
Jens Jensen's own favourite work (1915–20) in Austin — a prairie river, council rings and stone waterfalls interpreting the Illinois landscape. Free.
The 71-acre 1901 park named for the assassinated president — lagoon, trails and an outdoor ice rink. Free.
Home of the Bulls and Blackhawks; the 'Spirit' Michael Jordan statue stands in the atrium by Gate 4.
The White Sox's 1991 ballpark across 35th Street from old Comiskey, with the exploding scoreboard and fireworks after every Sox homer.

P.ad: Kirk Rd & Pine St, Batavia, IL 60510
P.w: The national particle-physics lab on the prairie — a bison herd since 1967, Wilson Hall and mathematical sculptures; grounds free with photo ID.

P.ad: 3624 S Dr Martin Luther King Jr Dr, Chicago, IL 60653
P.w: The 1889 Romanesque house where Ida B. Wells lived 1919–30 — a National Historic Landmark (private; view from the street).
Avondale's 1917 Polish 'cathedral' — a papal basilica since 2003 and the heart of Chicago's Polish Village.
Bucktown's block-long Polish Renaissance church (1920) modelled on St. Peter's, its dome ringed by angels.

P.ad: Mt. Baldy Beach, US-12, Michigan City, IN 46360
P.w: The 120-ft living dune at the east end of Indiana Dunes National Park — the largest moving dune on Indiana's shore (summit by ranger-led hike).

P.ad: 1 Heisman Harbor Rd (Washington Park), Michigan City, IN 46360
P.w: The 1858 Michigan City lighthouse, now a museum in Washington Park by the beach and harbour.
Starved Rock's quieter neighbour — canyon dells and waterfalls about two hours from Chicago.

P.n: Wolf Lake (William W. Powers State Recreation Area)
P.w: The 800-acre lake straddling the Illinois–Indiana line in Hegewisch — otters, beavers, swans and fishing amid the old steel landscape. Free.

P.ad: 222 W Merchandise Mart Plaza, Chicago, IL 60654
P.w: The 1930 Art Deco 'Mart' on the river — once the largest building in the world, with Jules Guérin murals inside and Art on the Mart projections on its facade at night.
Louis Sullivan's 1899–1904 Carson Pirie Scott store at State & Madison — the cast-iron prairie-foliage entrance rotunda is the masterpiece.
Atwood's 1895 terracotta-and-glass tower — a prototype of the glass skyscraper and the Chicago window (now a hotel).
Jeanne Gang's 2009 tower whose rippling white balconies look like water cascading down its sides.
Chicago's oldest continually operating hotel — the gilded lobby ceiling and Tiffany fittings; birthplace of the brownie.
The domed 1926 Beaux-Arts memorial in Lincoln Park — marble rotunda, Eugene Savage murals and heroic friezes; one of WTTW's 'Most Beautiful Places'. Free.
Caldwell's 1938 Prairie-style 'hidden garden' in Lincoln Park — stratified stone, a prairie river and a waterfall; a National Historic Landmark, open April–October. Free.
P.k: garden park prairie school landmark free

P.ad: 217 S Home Ave, Oak Park, IL 60302
P.w: George W. Maher's 1897 John Farson House — an early Prairie-style mansion and National Historic Landmark, open for tours.
Living-history village of 30 historic buildings and costumed interpreters telling a 19th-century Illinois town's story.
Ukrainian Village's storefront indie-rock club — cheap shows, free Mondays, a bar cat and the midwinter Music Frozen Dancing fest.
A century-old frame house tucked into an industrial corridor (once bootleggers' turf) — beloved for concerts, variety shows and comedy.
Wrigleyville's 1927 theatre turned rock club (since 1982) — midsize touring acts upstairs, Smart Bar downstairs.
Adler & Sullivan's 1890 synagogue turned the church where Thomas Dorsey's choir gave birth to gospel music; burned in 2006, its stone walls still stand (a gospel museum is planned).
Anthony Overton's 1929–31 Art Deco terracotta newspaper building in Bronzeville, now the Chicago Bee branch library.
The University of Chicago's always-free art museum in Edward Larrabee Barnes's limestone buildings.
Frank Lloyd Wright's 1897 Isidore Heller house in Hyde Park, a step toward the Prairie style (private; view from the street).
P.k: frank lloyd wright prairie school house

P.w: Chicago's oldest and largest not-for-profit theatre (1925), in the Loop theatre district.

P.ad: 800 E Grand Ave (Navy Pier), Chicago, IL 60611
P.w: The Tony-winning Shakespeare company at the end of Navy Pier.

P.ad: 20 N Upper Wacker Dr, Chicago, IL 60606
P.w: Samuel Insull's 1929 Art Deco 'throne' on the river, its gilded hall home to the Lyric Opera since 1954.
Orchestra Hall (1904) on Michigan Avenue, home of the world-famous Chicago Symphony Orchestra.
The German parish's Romanesque church rebuilt inside its fire-scarred walls after 1871 — Bavarian Baroque interior and Munich glass.
Chicago's largest cemetery (350 acres), entered through William Boyington's castle-like gate — Victorian monuments and mausoleums.

F.w: The Taylor Street original (1938) where the family claims the Italian beef was invented; the beef for every Al's is still roasted here. #1 on the Infatuation's Italian-beef ranking and a fixture of every Chicago beef list.

F.ad: 7500 W North Ave, Elmwood Park, IL 60707
F.w: Elmwood Park walk-up open since 1961 — Steve Dolinsky's (ABC7 Hungry Hound) #1 Italian beef in the suburbs, with an 'ambrosial' jus, and the lemon ice that closes every order.
Lincoln Park's pan-pizza bar whose pies are ringed with blackened, caramelized cheese — the deep dish many Chicagoans name first (Infatuation) and #8 on Time Out's citywide pizza ranking.
The family that helped invent deep dish (Lou worked at Uno before opening his own in 1971); Infatuation calls it the best version of the classic Chicago pie — sauce on top, flaky buttery crust.
Edgewater carryout doing a focaccia-like sourdough deep dish; on both the Infatuation deep-dish ranking and Time Out's top pizza list.
Pandemic-born Uptown pan-pizza shop in the Pequod's lineage — #2 on Time Out's citywide pizza ranking and on the Infatuation deep-dish list.
Ashburn's tavern-pizza shrine since the 1940s — #1 on Time Out's citywide pizza ranking ('the king of tavern-style') and the spot with the most 'best' nods in Chowhound's tavern-pizza research.
Family-run Lincoln Park pizzeria (since 1950) whose flaky, cracker-thin crust is on Time Out's top-pizza ranking and Chowhound's best tavern-style list.
Tiny West Town pizzeria in a former barbershop from veteran Chicago pizza makers — #3 on Time Out's citywide ranking, #1 on Chowhound's tavern list and an Esquire Best New Restaurant 2025.
Logan Square brewpub-bakery; on Time Out's top-pizza ranking and the only brewpub on Chowhound's tavern-pizza list.
The 1948 carhop drive-in under the two giant hot-dog mascots on the roof — on both the Infatuation and Time Out best-hot-dog lists.

F.ad: 2720 N River Rd, River Grove, IL 60171
F.w: River Grove stand (1946; here since 1950) — no seats, no ketchup; the gold standard of the Depression dog on both the Infatuation and Time Out hot-dog lists.
West Ridge stand famous since 1967 for its sign — a giant hot dog on a fork — and a char dog both the Infatuation and Time Out rank among the city's best.
Cheap, late Depression-dog stand on Armitage — on both the Infatuation and Time Out hot-dog lists.

F.ad: 1017 W Irving Park Rd, Chicago, IL 60613
F.w: Classic Wrigleyville hot-dog stand serving the North Side since 1975 — reviewed by the Infatuation and on Time Out's best-hot-dogs list.
Cash-only Marquette Park trailer open since 1972 that 'looks like a strong wind might blow it over' — on both the Infatuation and Time Out hot-dog lists.
Founded 1954 by the Lemons brothers and still family-run; South Side aquarium-smoker rib tips. 2025 James Beard America's Classics award. James Beard America's Classics Award, 2025.
Uptown Hong Kong barbecue house near Argyle, family-run since 1987; 2018 James Beard America's Classics award.
German restaurant and bar in the Loop since 1898 — its bar held Chicago's first post-Prohibition liquor license. A James Beard America's Classics honoree.
Smokehouse shack by the 95th Street bridge on the Calumet River since 1948, wood-smoking fish on site. A James Beard America's Classics honoree.

F.ad: 551 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60616 (relocating from 1250 S Union Ave)
F.w: Open around the clock since 1939 — the stand that claims the original Maxwell Street Polish. Time Out calls it the best Polish in the city; its pork chop sandwich is one of Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats. Note: UIC, its landlord, ordered it off 1250 S Union Ave by June 30, 2026; it is moving to 551 W 18th St in Pilsen with a fall 2026 reopening (Sun-Times 2026-05-08, Fox32, WGN) — check it is open before going.
'Home of the Jibarito': Juan 'Peter' Figueroa's Humboldt Park restaurant created the plantain sandwich in 1996. Tops the Infatuation's jibarito guide and Chicago Magazine's Iconic Eats.
Old Town rib tavern open since 1932 (a Sinatra hangout), neon beer signs intact — on the Infatuation's old-school list and Chicago Magazine's Iconic Eats for its baby backs.
Ice-cream parlor and candy shop at Armitage & Western since 1921 — the Infatuation's old-school list and Chicago Magazine's Iconic Eats (hot fudge sundae).
River North steakhouse in its wood-frame building since 1941 — as old-school as Chicago gets (Infatuation), rib eye on Chicago Magazine's Iconic Eats.
South Loop cafeteria deli since 1942, lunchroom of generations of politicians — reviewed by the Infatuation ('still great after 80 years') and on Chicago Magazine's Iconic Eats for its corned beef.
Family-run Archer Heights birrieria devoted to Jalisco-style roasted goat. Michelin Bib Gourmand; birria on Chicago Magazine's Iconic Eats.

F.ad: 430 N Michigan Ave (lower level), Chicago, IL 60611
F.w: Lower Michigan Avenue newspapermen's tavern since 1934 — 'cheezborger, cheezborger, no Pepsi, Coke' of SNL fame and the Cubs' goat curse.
Deep-dish institution since 1966 near the Mag Mile, its cornmeal-crust pies served in graffiti-covered booths diners are invited to sign.
The River North beef stand (since 1979) that inspired The Bear's Original Beef of Chicagoland — dipped beef with hot giardiniera.
Beverly's pink stand serving its five-flavour sliced cone since 1926 — a South Side institution (Choose Chicago) and one of Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.
Stephanie Izard's Randolph Street flagship (2010) that made the West Loop a dining district — the pig-face plate is one of Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.
Paul Kahan's cedar-lined Mediterranean wine bar (2003) — its chorizo-stuffed, bacon-wrapped dates are one of Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.
Greektown's taverna since 1971 — flaming saganaki ('Opa!') is one of Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.
Skokie deli opened in the 1960s as a hub for Holocaust survivors — one of Chicagoland's oldest Jewish delis; bagel and lox on Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.
Lincoln Park's late-night char-dog stand (to 4am weekends), as famous for the staff's good-natured verbal abuse as for its dogs.
Humboldt Park bakery run by the same family since 1911 — custom cakes, strudel, coffee cake and paczki.
The traders' bar in the Board of Trade lobby, notorious for a 'jack and coke' that's a giant cup of whiskey with the can on the side.
The taproom attached to Goose Island's production brewery (brewing here since 1995) — test batches and Bourbon County Stout rarities.
West Loop tasting-menu restaurant tied to a family farm — Chicago's only three-Michelin-star restaurant in the 2025 guide.
Grant Achatz's Lincoln Park landmark of modernist cooking, 20 years old — two Michelin stars in 2025 (down from three).

Lee Wolen's Lincoln Park flagship by the Steppenwolf — one Michelin star.

South Loop brewery whose dining room above the brewhouse holds one Michelin star.

Sujan Sarkar's River North modern-Indian tasting room — one Michelin star.
Chicago's newest one-star in the 2025 Michelin guide, which also gave it a Green Star for sustainable practice.

Sujan Sarkar's regional-Indian Lincoln Park restaurant — new Michelin Bib Gourmand 2025.

Noah Sandoval's hidden West Loop tasting room behind a freight elevator — two Michelin stars (2025).

Julia Momosé's Japanese cocktail bar and dining room in the West Loop — in the Michelin Guide.

Andrew Zimmerman's West Loop dining room in a 19th-century print shop — one Michelin star (2025).

River North live-fire Middle Eastern restaurant — Michelin Bib Gourmand.
All-plant kitchen named a Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).

Lakeview neighbourhood bistro with French-Canadian roots — Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).
Bridgeport gastropub — a Michelin Bib Gourmand in both the 2024 and 2025 Chicago lists.
Low-key Pilsen restaurant for Northern Thai fare — Michelin Bib Gourmand.
Logan Square's tiny, always-full New American — Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).
River North gastropub — Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).
Logan Square salumeria/café — Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).

Spanish restaurant on Michelin's 2024 Chicago Bib Gourmand list.
Tiny Lincoln Park–Lakeview room for Iberian-inspired seafood — Michelin Bib Gourmand 2024 and 2025.
Diana Dávila's Logan Square antojería — Michelin Bib Gourmand and one of Eater Chicago's 38 essential restaurants.
Wicker Park/Noble Square Asian-American small-plates spot — Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).
Uptown pizzeria-bistro on Clark St — Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).
Hyde Park Neapolitan pizzeria on 55th St — Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).
River West Korean-American restaurant (401 N Milwaukee) on Michelin's 2024 Chicago Bib Gourmand list.
Pilsen pub famous for its royal pies — Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).
French café-bar — Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).
Magnificent Mile Mediterranean small-plates room — Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).
Old Irving Park's benchmark barbecue — Michelin Bib Gourmand and one of Eater Chicago's 38 essential restaurants.
Logan Square Indian restaurant — Michelin Bib Gourmand and Eater Chicago 38.

Below-street River North tiki bar — #27 on the World's 50 Best Bars (2014).

Old Town dive by Second City — walls of regulars' portraits, a Bourdain favourite.
Tony Hu's original Chinatown Sichuan house, through a side gate off Archer.
Greek taverna just off Logan Square Park — in the Michelin Guide.
Boka Group's West Loop Japanese canteen with multiple kitchens (exec. chef Gene Kato) — in the Michelin Guide.
Chef Sangtae Park's intimate West Loop omakase — in the Michelin Guide.
Wicker Park retro luncheonette (One Off Hospitality) — in the Michelin Guide.
Chef Erick Williams's Hyde Park Southern restaurant within view of the University of Chicago — Michelin Bib Gourmand 2025; Eater Chicago 38.
Sichuan restaurant — Michelin Bib Gourmand 2024 and 2025.
Sleek Chinatown restaurant with a full bar — Michelin-listed; 'diners would do well to try the impressive specialty menu'.
Stylish Chinatown Square dim-sum standby, open 365 days — Michelin Bib Gourmand; Infatuation 7.8.
Gold Coast steakhouse Michelin calls Chicago's buzziest — in the Michelin Guide.
Gold Coast Mexican from the first Mexican-born chef to earn a Michelin star — in the Michelin Guide.
Swanky steakhouse in the InterContinental — in the Michelin Guide.
Streeterville two-storey townhouse for classical French — in the Michelin Guide.
Avondale live-fire restaurant added to the Michelin Guide Chicago 2024 (NBC Chicago).
Belmont Cragin Mexican restaurant known for its moles — in the Michelin Guide.
Paul McGee's Logan Square Polynesian tiki bar — Time Out Chicago's Best Single-Focus Bar.
Eight-seat former speakeasy in the Chicago Athletic Association — No. 38 on North America's 50 Best Bars.
Logan Square 'neo-dive' — Time Out Chicago Bar of the Year and No. 48 on North America's 50 Best Bars.
Andersonville Belgian beer bar — Time Out Chicago's Best Beer Bar; a fixture of Chicago craft-beer guides.
Humboldt Park Puerto Rican kitchen on Division Street (since the 1990s) where locals send first-time jibarito eaters; BYOB.
Pine-paneled little Jefferson Park hideaway run by the Lakony family; one critic's pierogi crawl of 10 spots rated its pierogi 'by far the best'.
Ukrainian Village deli at Chicago Ave & Hoyne opened in 1982 by Polish immigrant Kazimiera 'Kasia' Bober, whose award-winning pierogi reached United flights and presidents.
Andersonville bakery-café honouring the neighbourhood's Swedish roots (chef Bobby Schaffer mills his own flour).
Avondale bakery that supplies The Publican; owner Sarah Mispagel consulted on The Bear and its chocolate cake is on the menu.
Evanston bread bakery that grew from a farmers'-market stall.
Logan Square pie-and-biscuit shop with a popular patio.
Stephanie Hart's 75th Street bakery (James Beard nominee) — its caramel cake is one of Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.
Chatham soul-food institution opened 1986 by Josephine Wade — an Aretha Franklin favourite and a base for community organising.
Small-batch doughnut shop (with fried chicken) — Axios Chicago's pick for yeast-raised.
Roseland doughnut shop many call the best in Chicago — in Axios Chicago's 2026 donut face-off and Yelp's national top 100.
Bridgeport Italian institution since 1946 whose 1976 breaded steak sandwich Bourdain featured on Parts Unknown.
Chinatown's oldest bakery (1986), Hong Kong recipes, 100+ goods baked daily; Infatuation 8.8.
Wicker Park's modern Greek — no Greektown kitsch, refined regional cooking.
Greektown restaurant (1997) with one of Chicago's best-known outdoor patios.
Korean institution since 1988 on the old Lincoln Ave Koreatown strip.
Classic charcoal Korean barbecue in Lincoln Square since 1992.
Beverly Kim and Johnny Clark's highly personal Korean-American restaurant in Avondale — one of the most creative rooms in town.
West Loop diner whose cheeseburger Thrillist ranked among America's best — the most hyped burger in Chicago.
Avondale heavy-metal burger bar (2005) — its Kuma burger was named America's best by The Daily Meal.
Taylor Street summer-only Italian-ice stand since 1954 — one of Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.

F.ad: 1073 W Vernon Park Pl, Chicago, IL 60607
F.w: Little Italy tavern founded 1930 by Joseph and Teresa DiBuono — James Beard America's Classics Award (2008).
Ukrainian Village's Old-World Ukrainian kitchen (opened 2016) — the Infatuation's pick for a varenyky-and-vodka night.
North Center Northern-Thai specialist (chef-owner Kritsana Moungkeow) — #8 on Time Out's Thai list.
Wrigleyville Thai ('Thailand's Authentic Cuisine') — order off the translated Thai menu; #7 on Time Out's Thai list.
Logan Square ramen counter from Mike Satinover — Reddit's 'Ramen Lord' of r/ramen — on Bon Appétit's 20 best new restaurants of 2024 and the NYT's 25 best in Chicago.
River North French restaurant (Carrie Nahabedian) — a 2015 James Beard Award recipient and on the NYT's 25 best in Chicago.
Bridgeport's tavern-style institution since 1960 — greasy, generously topped thin pies cut in squares, counter service, cash only.
South Siders' pick for the city's best beef — one of the biggest sandwiches in town, thicker slices that stay tender (Infatuation 8.0).
Beverly's wood-panelled burger shop since 1942 — fresh-ground round on a feather-light bun, fries cooked in beef tallow.
Evanston's old-school burger counter (2009) — the North Shore's burger benchmark on Infatuation's and Time Out's Evanston lists.
Pilsen carnitas house opened by Pedro Duarte in 1981 — pork cooked in its own fat, sold by weight; weekend lines out the door.
Cicero corner grocery turned Italian deli-pizzeria, run by Neapolitan immigrant Joe Quercia since 1973 — hot-table Italian, pizza and some of the area's best gelato.
Live-fire Greek from James Beard winner Jimmy Bannos Jr. — named to the New York Times' best-restaurants-in-America list.
Bucktown Chinese-American cocktail bar with a Michelin Bib Gourmand.
Hyde Park cafeteria since 1921, one of the oldest in the US — Barack Obama's regular, his orders still on the board. Cash only.

F.ad: 3511 S Martin Luther King Dr, Chicago, IL 60653
F.w: Senegalese family restaurant (2004, Bronzeville since 2015) — called one of the city's best African restaurants; South Side Weekly's 'Best Resurrection' after a fire.
Chicago-style aquarium-smoker barbecue, in Bronzeville since 2015 — a Choose Chicago South Side pick. Cash only.
Bronzeville soul-food dining room since 1993 — Roadfood rates it 'Excellent / Worth a Detour'.
Evanston barbecue institution of the late Hecky Powell — the North Shore's rib-tip and sauce benchmark (Axios rib-tip Food Fight).
The 1960 Wilmette original of the North Shore pancake family (in Ordinary People) — Zagat's 'best breakfast, bar none'.
Opened 1930 — the oldest continuously operating barbecue restaurant in the Chicago area, on Thatcher Avenue since the 1940s.
Andersonville's tiny Swedish breakfast room with Viking art — the last of the neighbourhood's old Swedish diners.
The 1971 original of Lou Malnati's — where the family's buttercrust deep dish began, before it became Chicago's best-known deep-dish name.
Berwyn roots-music club and tavern (FitzGerald family since 1980, a music hall since the 1930s) — in 2025 the first Illinois music venue on the National Register.
Pullman smokehouse of Dominique Leach, 2023 'Master of 'Cue' on Food Network's BBQ Brawl — one of the city's best barbecue spots.
Little Village's unlikely al pastor champion — a Chinese-Thai takeout counter whose trompo makes some of the best al pastor in Chicago.
The 1950 tortilla maker's cafeteria on 26th Street — fresh tortillas off the line and one of Little Village's best Mexican restaurants.
Austin's soul-food cafeteria (1997) of Mississippi-born MacArthur Alexander — a West Side institution whose regulars included Barack Obama.
University Village corner stand (since 1929) — the Infatuation calls its jus the best in Chicago; cash-only ice counter next door.
Pilsen's Green-Restaurant-certified bar and cultural space — solar panels, salvaged fittings, a bar made from a bowling lane.
Where Ike Sewell's 1943 pizzeria is credited with launching Chicago deep dish — the original still stands at Ohio & Wabash.
River North steakhouse (1987) named for the Cubs broadcaster, in a building once home to Capone enforcer Frank Nitti.
Rush Street power steakhouse since 1989 — consistently among the top-grossing independent restaurants in the US.
One of America's oldest continuously operating lunch-car diners (1926), hauled to Kenosha by six horses — on the National Register.
Milwaukee's neon-lit custard stand since the 1940s — said to have inspired Arnold's on Happy Days.

F.ad: 4629 N Port Washington Rd, Glendale, WI 53212
F.w: Glendale diner (1936) thought to have created the Wisconsin butter burger.

F.ad: N Clark St just north of Foster Ave, Andersonville, Chicago
F.w: The 'Anchor of Andersonville' since 1934 — founded by Swedish immigrant Simon Lundberg over his Prohibition-era No Name Club speakeasy.
Puerto Rican-owned bakery-café on Paseo Boricua a block from Humboldt Park — some of the city's best Puerto Rican coffee and pastries.
Paul Kahan's honky-tonk taco and whiskey bar at the Damen-Milwaukee crossroads of Wicker Park, with its packed summer patio.
The big Balmoral brewery and taproom (2017) of Half Acre, a staple of Chicago craft brewing since 2006.
Uptown's late-night honky-tonk — one of Chicago's last straight-up country bars, closed in 2016 and revived in 2018.
Lakeview dive at Clark & Belmont since the 1950s — Irish whiskey selection, a dark lore, and a stop on Anthony Bourdain's The Layover.
Six-table Edgewater counter where masa is patted and griddled to order — called the best huaraches in Chicago. Cash only.
Cash-only North Center taqueria — 'some of the freshest tacos in town' (Time Out); the Infatuation rates its carne asada 8.1.
Paul Kahan's 2008 Fulton Market beer hall of pork, oysters and beer — the restaurant that helped turn the meatpacking district into a dining destination.
Chicago's oldest Italian restaurant (1927), opened by Lucca-born Alfredo Capitanini and run by the fourth generation — a pre-opera Loop institution.
James Beard-winning chef Sarah Grueneberg's West Loop pasta house (2015), with sheets rolled and hung daily in view of the counter.
